rows.title: Back-off sets are written to training history like any set
rows.detail: method Primer + Paused Top/Back-Offs; 3 sets logged (200 top, 2 back-offs at 170): 3 records in pa_hist

rows.title: Evidence, target, coach summary and budget reads never delete or alter back-off records
Volume accounting counts back-offs: session.setCount and completion.performed include every logged set
History views still show every set: the PREVIOUS line lists top set and back-offs; chart data has all rows
A full backup contains the back-off records and validates
Back-off sets stay identifiable for future back-off analysis (method + set number + load + reps + session + date on every record)
Back-offs are absent from top-set comparisons
rows.detail: evidence series for the exercise: {"name":"SYSTEM","vals":[]} (top set only: 200 x 5 = 233)

rows.title: A legacy record with no setNumber is treated as a top set, never as a back-off
rows.detail: isBackoffRecord(no setNumber) = false; the original 2.3 app already wrote setNumber, so every stored record has one

rows.title: An unfinished draft keeps every logged set: in pa_hist, in the session record, and in a full backup
The draft set is excluded from completed-session evidence
rows.detail: evidence values [] (a draft 100 x 5 would be 117)

rows.title: After a reload the draft resumes with its set; once finished all its sets are complete-session records and no longer excluded as a draft
rows.detail: sets 2, status complete, still treated as draft false; evidence values [] (the engine reports no series until an exercise has 2 or more dated exposures, so values may be empty here)

rows.title: NEXT-target text is not covered by the draft exclusion: it reads the newest session of the series even if that session is an unfinished draft
rows.detail: NEXT shows "60 lb • earn reps/quality before +5 lb" while its newest session is an abandoned draft with one light set (evidence decision itself ignores that draft)
